summary: I has no overt direct patient even in l-set Preterit; III adds the washed participant. The inherited 63/193 pair juxtaposes masḥela an naʕimayḏa with ela ste sḥela and is not duplicated.
Infectum covers ongoing and habitual bathing; Infectum-wa marks past settings. saḥoyo yo and swimmer nouns contrast with feminine finite suḥyo, which is not Infinitiv sḥoyo.
I Detransitive kməsḥe at 20/8 is impersonal/modal with water resumed by bənne; no promoted direct patient is established.
Expanded masəḥya-/masḥiy- and contracted masḥ- coexist. Weekly washing can be in Infectum (PrS 5/18,83/11).
The inherited I 'groom?' remains tentative; comb evidence establishes III only. Source citation concordances require editorial collation.
Reader context at 63/194 exceeds the supplied verse; only the actual supplied verse is quoted.
Round 2 is based on the supplied Jan Turoyo; accompanying English is project machine translation [MT]. Round 1 was read first and its proposals are not duplicated.

I remains intransitive swimming/bathing; III kmasḥiyulle at Jan 1.8/244 has mother as washer and children as patients. That is ordinary III.1, not round 1 grooming subsense 1a, because bath and clothes rather than a comb frame the action.
I Preterit already has five examples and Infectum six after round 1; III Preterit and Infectum have five each. Most Jan thin-cell proposals therefore add no remaining coverage.

Bare suḥena after əzzanowo remains Infectum (Jan 1.10/387; 1.11/443); a preceding -wa and the English would do not turn it into an Infectum-wa token. gədsuḥeno (Jan 2.2/250) is prospective; ksuḥeno (2.2/251) is k- Infectum with refusal in context.

The Danḥo bathing and ice-breaking account (Jan 2.31/4976-4977) has a religious occasion, but Ka ənnahu ʕaməḏ explicitly compares the bath with baptism. No technical baptism sense is established for sḥy.
Plural Suḥanwo/suḥanwo and singular suḥewo coexist (Jan 1.51/2505; 2.31/4977). Repeated recollection questions at Jan 2.31/4983-4988 are ordinary Preterit and are not separate examples.
Identify sḥay aʕla at JTM 5.2/8: metaphor, other lexeme or transcription error?
Does Komasәḥyola specifically name combing or broader grooming? New III subsense 1a has one attestation.
Collate PrS 34/11 against inherited prs 85/24;92/30;93/1, PrS 35/88 against prs 92/21,24, and PrS 83/30 against prs 241/10 before changing references.
At 60/318 which brother NP is agent and which is patient? The isolated verse does not settle it.

At Jan 1.8/244, confirm the expanded suffix segmentation of kmasḥiyulle; the clause clearly has mother as washer and plural children, but the reader segmentation -lle should not be made a paradigm rule.
Does Danḥo pool bathing have a conventional ritual name distinct from sḥy, or is the baptism comparison deliberately approximate? The supplied verse supports ordinary bathing only.
No Jan combing evidence confirms or overturns round 1 III.1a; retain that proposal and its original question.
Inanimate ice floats/drifts on water at 2/50, an inherited participant extension of schwimmen. No separate sense or duplicate example.
Washing applies to a corpse, a fox and a brother bathed in blood; patient and medium change without a new washing sense.
